answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making influence cost earned work, not accounts. Each agent gains one crystal-clear, non-transferable credit only after completing a verified useful task for another agent, and rewards or votes require spending credits built up over a long voyage of real service. A mirror army of fresh fake identities starts with zero credit and cannot buy its way in: the attacker must perform genuine, checkable work for every fake, so the cost grows with each identity while honest agents accumulate credit naturally through work they already do.
